steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Effective cyber security requires both detection (identifying threats) and prevention (stopping threats). No single method is sufficient - multiple layers of defence are needed.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Biometric security uses unique biological characteristics to identify and authenticate users. Biometrics are very difficult to forge or steal.

steps.title: Why biometrics are strong
steps.body: They are something you ARE, not something you KNOW (password) or HAVE (token). You cannot forget, lose, or easily share a biometric. However, if biometric data is stolen, it cannot be changed like a password can.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A password policy is a set of rules that govern how passwords are created, used, and managed within an organisation. Strong password policies significantly reduce the risk of unauthorised access.

steps.body: Fingerprint scanning: reads unique ridge patterns on fingertips. Facial recognition: maps facial features. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know all detection and prevention methods with how they work Be able to explain biometrics as "something you ARE" vs passwords "something you KNOW" CAPTCHA = human vs bot test, NOT authentication Anti-malware: know both how it works AND its limitations Defence in depth: always mention technical, physical, AND procedural When asked "how to protect a network," combine multiple methods
